role: single guard reaction on the defender at the moment a blow is blocked (frequent, about 0.5 s)
style: stylized action-game energy guard, original synthetic design
dominant_shape: a shallow convex guard disc standing beside the defender on the attacker's side (+X), yawed (0,58,0) so it reads as a vertical ellipse; outline first, then a flowing blue face that splits into six plate sectors

beats.name: raise (earliest readable)
beats.expect: A thin pale arc on the +X side of the dummy, open at the top: the lower half of the outline drawing itself up both sides. No fill and no white star yet.

beats.name: contact
beats.expect: A short white anamorphic star at chest height on the disc with a small blue bloom under it; the outline is closed and the blue face is appearing behind the star. The star is the brightest thing in the frame.

beats.name: body takes over
beats.expect: The white star is gone. The blue face keeps its bright rim and thin centre; a ripple ring spreads from the contact point and the mottled noise has moved compared with f5. Head and torso of the dummy readable beside and through the disc.

beats.name: gaps open
beats.expect: The face is eroded into holes and six plate sectors with dark gaps between them are visible, the widest gap at the top under the contact point; the sectors are saturated blue with dimmer navy edges, no brighter than the f10 face and never near-white; blue-grey chips appear.

beats.name: exit start
beats.expect: The whole face and ripples are gone; only the separating blue plate sectors and chips remain.

beats.name: exit midpoint (last intentional residue)
beats.expect: Sectors are visibly farther from the disc centre than at f16, tilted differently from each other, the same blue but dimmer (fading) and more eroded; still readable as a modest blue tail; chips are below the contact height.

beats.name: clear
beats.expect: No effect pixels remain; the dummy stands alone on the stage.

layer_plan.name: 0:Guard plane
layer_plan.role: invisible pivot: places the disc at +X of the defender and yaws it (0,58,0) so every plane layer shares one tilted plane
layer_plan.exit: no pixels; node life ends at absolute f28

layer_plan.name: 0:Guard plane/0:Outline draw
layer_plan.role: anticipation: thin shield outline rising from the bottom up both sides (angle sweep 180->0 / 180->360)
layer_plan.exit: fades from f4, gone by absolute f7

layer_plan.name: 0:Guard plane/1:Guard face
layer_plan.role: body: convex blue disc with pale rim and thin centre in fixed Ring vertex colours (no colour animation); the noise mask flows round and outward, small give under the blow, then erodes into holes with a pale edge and fades
layer_plan.primitive: Ring (fixed outer/center/inner colours) + alpha T_NoiseTile02 scroll + EaseInQuadratic cutoff + edge
layer_plan.exit: eroded and faded, gone by absolute f18

layer_plan.name: 0:Guard plane/2:Face ripple
layer_plan.role: body motion: two ripple rings spreading over the face from the contact point (born f5 and f8)

layer_plan.name: 0:Guard plane/3:Plate shard 1
layer_plan.role: exit break-up: 46-degree sector centred at 30 degrees; fixed Ring vertex colours (saturated blue band, dimmer navy outer/inner edge, emissive 1.0, below the face's value); separates, tumbles, dims by fade and erosion (no colour animation)
layer_plan.primitive: Ring sector (fixed outer/center/inner colours) + travel + spin + cutoff
layer_plan.exit: born f13, gone by absolute f28

layer_plan.role: invisible unrotated pivot at the contact's world position so spray boxes stay in world axes
layer_plan.exit: no pixels; node life ends at absolute f29

layer_plan.name: 1:Contact point/0:Contact glint
layer_plan.role: contact: short white star of the blocked blow (core value)

layer_plan.name: 1:Contact point/1:Contact bloom
layer_plan.role: contact support: small blue bloom under the star so the contact is white over blue, not a white disc

layer_plan.name: 1:Contact point/2:Deflect sparks
layer_plan.role: secondary: six short glints deflected back toward the attacker (+X) and up, eased out

layer_plan.name: 1:Contact point/3:Plate chips
layer_plan.role: matter: seven small alpha-blended blue-grey chips spread over the plate at the break, falling
layer_plan.primitive: debris (Sprite T_Shard01, Blend) with a 0.4 spawn sphere
layer_plan.exit: born f13, gone by absolute f29

acceptance: f2: the outline is an open arc (lower part only) beside the dummy, not a closed ring and not a filled disc
f4-f8: the white contact star is the brightest element and is gone by f9; no white mass remains at f10
f10: the dummy's head and torso stay readable; the disc sits beside the character (attacker side), not over it
f5 vs f10 vs f14: the face visibly changes (ripple at a different radius, noise moved, holes appearing); it is not a static disc that only fades
f16: at least four dark gaps divide the plate into separate pieces
f13-f23: plate pieces are saturated blue with dimmer edges, never near-white and never brighter than the f10 face; the f4-f8 contact star stays the single brightest event
f23: pieces are farther from the disc centre than at f16, tilted differently, dimmer and more eroded but still a visible blue tail; chips below contact height
f30: nothing of the effect remains
In greyscale the order reads: white star > pale rim and outline > blue face > navy pieces and chips
avoid: A tinted solid disc or dome covering the dummy
A held barrier that stays up after the reaction; anything still visible at f30
An attack-style blast: a large or long white flash, a big shock ring, smoke
A recolour of the Shield Dome sphere and its fragments
Sparks or chips sprayed evenly in all directions like fireworks
Plate pieces popping in brighter or bigger than the face they replace
